sources.title: Developing Skilled Defencemen — Overview
sources.use: Supports the stated coaching principle. The setup, alternatives and suggested answers are original experimental coaching synthesis, not source-certified.

replacement.limits: Age adaptation and tactical alternatives await coaching review. Static setup: no skating speed, interception timing or uniquely optimal route has been validated. Positional references are examples, not scored targets.

questions.prompt: Which teammate is on the opposite side of the net from YOU?
questions.explanation: D2 and YOU are on opposite sides of Navy’s net.

questions.prompt: Select two checks before using the permitted reverse.

options.text: Whether the first planned pass must be completed
Whether pressure can reach the reverse route

questions.explanation: The reverse is an option only if its receiver and route remain usable.

options.text: Use the reverse only if that route remains available

questions.explanation: The routine supports a decision, not an automatic reverse every time pressure appears.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to an example spot for protecting possession while looking toward D2.
questions.explanation: A tighter position toward the middle of the net can change the angle you present to pressure. Actual goalie and defender locations still matter.

questions.prompt: If D2 is closely marked before you release, what is sensible?

options.text: Reverse automatically because it was the original plan
Pass through D2’s marker without checking
Reassess a hold or another outlet

questions.explanation: A closed second option means another read is needed; holding may be useful if possession can be protected.

questions.prompt: Why is “the first outlet is closed” insufficient by itself to choose a reverse?
questions.explanation: A different lane and a prepared receiver must also exist. Mention pressure on D2 or time to protect the puck.

questions.prompt: What does Gold 1’s position between YOU and W change?

options.text: The direct W outlet is restricted
The puck is already in the neutral zone

questions.explanation: Gold 1 occupies the direct lane to W, so that pass needs a different angle or protection; if Gold 1 moves away, recheck W.

questions.prompt: Which two details should accompany a reverse call?

options.text: Whether the reverse lane is open
That D2 is automatically open because Gold 1 is near W

questions.explanation: D2’s side and the lane’s current access tell teammates what the reverse can solve; faceoff history does not.

questions.prompt: Move YOU closer to the back of the net while keeping Gold 1’s pressure side visible.
questions.explanation: The behind-net position can change Gold 1’s angle and keep D2 in view; if Gold 1 follows, protect before choosing the reverse.

questions.prompt: Why does a closed strong-side outlet permit a reverse without requiring it?
questions.explanation: The closure removes one lane while D2’s side and pressure determine whether the reverse helps; if the reverse is covered too, protect or wait.
